subject: Business
title: Nearshoring: Bringing Production Closer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nearshoring: Bringing Production Closer.

hook.text: After COVID delays, US companies moved production from China to Mexico. Transit time dropped from 30 days to 3.

buildup.text: Nearshoring means relocating production to a country closer to your customers, trading lower wages for shorter lead times.

discovery.text: Mexico became the US's top trading partner in 2023, overtaking China for the first time in two decades.

twist.text: Nearshoring isn't always cheaper. Higher wages and infrastructure gaps can offset the savings from shorter shipping.

climax.text: The calculation changed: resilience and speed now matter as much as cost. Post-pandemic supply chains value reliability.

punchline.text: Cheap is far away. Reliable is close. Companies are choosing reliable.

quiz.question: Why are companies nearshoring production?
options: To reduce transit times and increase supply chain resilience
Because foreign labor is always more expensive
To comply with new international shipping laws

details.summary: Nearshoring moves production from distant low-cost countries to closer geographic locations, trading lower labor costs for reduced lead times, lower transportation expenses, and better supply chain control. It has accelerated as companies rebalance efficiency against resilience.
details.whyItMatters: Post-pandemic supply chain disruptions and rising geopolitical tensions accelerated the nearshoring trend. Companies are rethinking decades of offshoring as shorter supply chains prove more reliable and total costs increasingly favor regional
takeaways: Nearshoring shortens lead times and reduces transportation complexity
Rising overseas labor costs narrow the gap with nearer alternatives
Geopolitical risks and pandemic disruptions accelerated the nearshoring trend

faq.question: What is the difference between nearshoring, reshoring, and friendshoring?
faq.answer: Nearshoring moves production to nearby countries like US companies moving from China to Mexico. Reshoring brings production back to the home country. Friendshoring sources from geopolitically aligned nations to reduce political risk regardless of geographic proximity.

faq.question: What factors are driving the nearshoring trend?
faq.answer: Rising overseas labor costs, expensive trans-Pacific shipping, pandemic-exposed supply vulnerabilities, geopolitical tensions between major trading blocs, need for faster time-to-market, growing automation reducing labor cost advantages, and ESG pressure to reduce transport emissions.
